extracted.intended_audience: institutions of higher education (IHEs), local education agencies (LEAs), Title IX Coordinators, institutional legal counsel, and stakeholders commenting on/implementing Title IX regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory preamble and regulatory analysis responding to public comments on the Department's final Title IX regulations, including definitions, scope, cost assumptions, and procedural obligations for recipients. Focuses on how and when recipients must investigate and adjudicate allegations of sexual harassment and related regulatory impact assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear policies and procedures balancing supportive environment and due process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must have clear policies and procedures in place to promote a safe and supportive environment while also ensuring due process protections are applied whenever the recipient investigates and adjudicates sexual harassment allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes consistent and supportive responses to reports rather than compelling reporting. The goal is not to reduce investigations but to ensure clear guidelines under Title IX so complainants and respondents have clarity about the school's burdens and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'formal complaint'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'formal complaint' in §106.30 is revised to mean a document filed by a complainant, or signed by the Title IX Coordinator, requesting that the recipient investigate sexual harassment allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal complaint may be filed in person, by mail, or email; and the formal complaint may be a document or electronic submission with the complainant's physical or digital signature or otherwise indicating that the complainant is the person filing the formal complaint. This revision was made to address confusion about what constitutes a formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'sexual harassment' includes Clery Act/VAWA terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised the definition of 'sexual harassment' to include sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, and stalking as defined in the Clery Act and VAWA, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change broadens the set of incidents considered sexual harassment under §106.30 and was used to update estimates of the number of investigations; however, recipients' obligations under Title IX remain distinct from Clery Act obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger for Title IX investigation (formal complaint requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under these final regulations, a recipient must conduct an investigation (part of the grievance process in §106.45) after a formal complaint is filed by a complainant or signed by the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the procedural trigger for Title IX grievance processing; the Department notes this trigger differs from Clery Act reporting obligations and that recipients may still have separate obligations under other laws or institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections regarding cross-examination and party participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants are not required to participate in cross-examination, and decision-makers are prohibited from basing a determination regarding responsibility on the absence of a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a complainant opts not to participate in cross-examination, they may still receive supportive measures. The Department rejects claims that cross-examination requirements force complainant participation and recognizes advisors may perform cross-examination without compelling the complainant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'education program or activity' and jurisdiction (on- and off-campus incidents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must respond to allegations of sexual harassment in their education program or activity whether the alleged harassment occurs on campus or off campus; the final regulations include incidents occurring in buildings owned or controlled by student organizations officially recognized by a postsecondary institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarifies these rules do not categorically exclude off-campus allegations. Because data granularity is limited, the Department used Clery Act geographic categories (including noncampus/public property) conservatively when revising estimates of investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to analyze and allocate resources for jurisdictional determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may need to expend resources to determine whether a particular incident occurred within the recipient's education program or activity; the Department added time for Title IX Coordinators and investigators to engage in such analyses in approximately 50 percent of incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new cost category was added in the RIA to capture recipient efforts for jurisdictional analysis; this affects the overall cost estimates of implementing the grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline estimation and revision of number of investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised its estimate of the baseline number of investigations currently occurring at IHEs to 5.70 investigations per institution per year and the estimated number of formal complaints after implementation to 3.82.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These revisions resulted from commenter input and adjustments to definitions/scope; the Department used multiple data sources and sensitivity analyses to justify changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of publicly available data and transparency of assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department relied on publicly available data sources and clearly identified data and assumptions in the NPRM to allow public assessment of the validity of assumptions and estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department provided alternative estimates in a Sensitivity Analysis and requested the public submit alternative data to improve baseline estimates; transparency of underlying calculations was emphasized as good practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use and acknowledged limitations of Clery Act, CRDC, and YRBS data
rubrics_metrics.description: Clery Act, CRDC, and YRBS each provide context but have limitations (e.g., underreporting, participation bias, lack of granularity) that affect their suitability for estimating investigation rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department considers CRDC more likely to capture incidents recipients are required to investigate, but acknowledges data quality issues. Commenters urged against uncritical reliance on these datasets; the Department documented limitations and chose sources it judged most appropriate while requesting better data where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment of estimates using Clery Act-derived multipliers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department used 2017 Clery Act data to derive a multiplier (2.416) to adjust initial estimates to account for inclusion of dating violence, domestic violence, and stalking alongside sexual assault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the Department found ~1.416 reported incidents of dating violence/domestic violence/stalking for every incident of sexual assault and multiplied prior estimates accordingly to generate a revised baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost assumptions and wage-rate sourcing (attorney and staff hourly rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department used Bureau of Labor Statistics median hourly wage rates for attorneys in the education sector (and other BLS wage rates) when estimating costs; commenters argued local attorney rates may be much higher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department defends use of BLS as standard practice for such estimates but recognizes that institutions with no in-house counsel or in high-cost regions may face higher actual costs; sensitivity analyses can capture some variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for institutional variation and outliers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department recognizes wide variation across institutions (e.g., large IHEs investigate many more matters than small/community colleges) and attempts to estimate a reasonable average across all recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses included grouping recipients (e.g., analytical group 3) and sensitivity analyses to capture heterogeneity; commenters pointing to high-volume outliers were acknowledged but treated as not representative of the national average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions' discretion to investigate beyond Title IX obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the final regulations do not require investigation of incidents outside a recipient's education program or activity, institutions' own student conduct codes or obligations (e.g., under the Clery Act) may compel them to continue investigating such incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes some institutions will not experience reductions in investigations because they will continue to process certain off-campus incidents under other policies; such effects were included in the initial analysis where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include costs for development/revision of grievance procedures and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated implementation costs include developing or revising grievance procedures and training Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, or persons designated to facilitate informal resolution processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department's cost estimates specifically account for procedural development and required training to ensure compliance with the final grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions about delegation of administrative tasks and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's analysis assumed certain administrative tasks associated with coordinating the grievance process could be delegated to positions such as administrative assistants or office administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted many Title IX Coordinators lack administrative assistants; the Department acknowledges this may raise or lower costs depending on whether coordinators perform tasks themselves or delegate, and that wage-rate differentials affect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: No federal compulsion for individuals to report; focus on recipient response
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not require individuals to report incidents; the regulatory focus is ensuring recipients respond consistently and appropriately when they do receive reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble rejects the premise that the regulations compel reporting and reiterates supportive measures and due process protections for complainants and respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender-identity coverage despite omission of the word 'transgender'
rubrics_metrics.description: The omission of the word 'transgender' in the NPRM does not indicate exclusion from Title IX protections; the regulations focus on prohibited conduct and anyone may experience sexual harassment as defined in §106.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department points commenters to the 'Gender-based harassment' subsection for fuller explanation and confirms protections apply by conduct, not solely by particular identity labels.
